D005-D007_h001.question:
I’m a robotics engineer, so I’m used to thinking in terms of systems and logic, but the last two months haven’t felt logical at all.

It started with this fixed idea I can’t shake that something terrible is coming, like the world is winding down. It’s not just climate change or the news—I feel absolutely certain there’s some kind of collapse coming soon, like everything is hollowed out already. I catch myself checking emergency supplies, planning escape routes, even though I know on some level it sounds irrational.

Around the same time, I began seeing things that no one else seems to notice—people or shapes in the corners of rooms, almost like silhouettes made of static. At work, I sometimes see someone standing by a lab bench, but when I look directly, no one’s there. It’s unsettling, but I can still do my job; I just feel on edge.

Emotionally, I’ve been more down than usual—low energy, less interest in my projects, pulling back from my wife and friends. Some days it’s heavier than others, but I can’t really map out how it lines up with the other stuff; it all kind of blurs together over these weeks.
D005-D007_h001.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D005-D007_h001.answer: A & B. Schizophrenia & Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D005-D007_h002.question:

Mood-wise, I’ve been pretty low on and off—more tired, not really excited about projects I’d normally love, sleeping more when I can. I’m not sure how much of that is just stress or burnout versus whatever else is going on.

D005-D007_h003.question:

D005-D007_h004.question:
